questions.text: Which formal element describes how light or dark something is?
questions.solution: Tone is the lightness or darkness of a colour or shade
questions.hint: Shading with a pencil changes this element

feedback: Texture is how something feels or looks like it would feel

questions.text: Which formal element describes how a surface feels, or looks as if it would feel? Give the element.
questions.solution: Texture is the surface quality of something: rough, smooth, bumpy and so on
questions.hint: Think of the difference between sandpaper and silk

questions.text: What is a design or motif that is repeated called?
questions.solution: A pattern is a repeated design, shape or motif, as in wallpaper or fabric
questions.hint: Think of wallpaper or a tartan scarf

questions.text: What is the empty space around and between objects in an artwork called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Negative space is the space around and between the subjects of an image
questions.hint: The objects themselves are the positive space

feedback.positive space: Positive space is the area taken up by the objects themselves

questions.text: In a perspective drawing, which line shows the viewer's eye level?
questions.solution: The horizon line shows eye level; vanishing points sit on it
questions.hint: At the seaside, it is where the sea seems to meet the sky

questions.text: In one-point perspective, where do the parallel lines that go away from the viewer meet?
questions.solution: In one-point perspective, receding parallel lines meet at one vanishing point on the horizon line
questions.hint: Think about railway lines going into the distance

options: At the bottom of the page
At two points off the page
At a single vanishing point on the horizon line

questions.text: Which statement about shape and form is accurate?
questions.solution: A shape is flat (2D), such as a circle; a form has volume (3D), such as a sphere
questions.hint: Compare a circle with a ball

options: Shape is two-dimensional; form is three-dimensional
Shape is three-dimensional; form is two-dimensional
Shape and form both mean colour
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which statement about actual texture and implied (visual) texture is accurate?
questions.solution: Actual texture is real and can be touched; implied texture is drawn or painted to look textured
questions.hint: Could you feel the texture of fur drawn in pencil?

options: Implied texture can be felt; actual texture only looks textured
Actual texture can be felt; implied texture only looks textured
Both can only be seen in sculpture
Both mean the same as tone
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which statement about one-point and two-point perspective is accurate?
questions.solution: One-point has a single vanishing point; two-point has two vanishing points on the horizon line
questions.hint: The number in the name gives a clue

options: One-point uses two vanishing points; two-point uses one
Two-point perspective has no horizon line
One-point uses one vanishing point; two-point uses two, often for drawing the corner of a building
One-point perspective is only used for portraits

questions.text: Which type of perspective makes distant objects look paler, bluer and less detailed? Give the term.
questions.solution: Aerial (atmospheric) perspective shows distance by making far objects paler, bluer and less detailed
questions.hint: It is caused by the air between the viewer and distant hills

feedback.linear perspective: Linear perspective uses lines and vanishing points, not colour and detail

questions.text: What is the focal point of a composition?
questions.solution: The focal point is the centre of interest that the viewer notices first
questions.hint: Which part of a painting grabs your attention straight away?

options: The lightest colour in the picture
The area that draws the viewer's eye first

questions.text: Which drawing technique shortens an object that points towards the viewer, such as an outstretched arm, to create depth? Give the term.
questions.solution: Foreshortening shortens objects that point towards or away from the viewer
questions.hint: The object looks 'shortened' at the front

questions.text: Which term describes the size of parts compared with each other, such as the head compared with the body?
questions.solution: Proportion is the relationship in size between parts of a whole
questions.hint: Think about getting the size of the head right in a figure drawing

questions.text: What does 'composition' mean in art?
questions.solution: Composition is the arrangement of the elements within an artwork
questions.hint: Think about where things are placed in the picture

options: How the parts of an artwork are arranged
The colours mixed on the palette

questions.text: In a portrait drawing of a face looking straight ahead, where are the eyes usually placed?
questions.solution: The eyes are roughly halfway between the top of the head and the chin
questions.hint: Measure from the top of the head to the chin

options: About a quarter of the way down from the top
Near the very top of the head
About three quarters of the way down

questions.text: An artist divides a picture into thirds both across and down and places the subject on one of the lines. Which guideline is this?
questions.solution: The rule of thirds places key subjects along the third lines or where they cross, for a balanced composition
questions.hint: Photographers often use this guideline, imagining a noughts-and-crosses grid over the view

questions.text: A drawing of a street has the lines of all the buildings heading towards one point in the distance. Which technique is this?
questions.solution: Lines meeting at a single point on the horizon is one-point perspective
questions.hint: How many points do the lines meet at?

questions.text: An artist draws an object with one unbroken line, without lifting the pencil from the paper. Give the term for this kind of drawing.
questions.solution: A continuous line drawing is made without lifting the pen or pencil
questions.hint: The line never stops

questions.text: A painting uses strong contrast between very light and very dark areas, as in Caravaggio's work. What is this called?
questions.solution: Chiaroscuro (Italian for 'light-dark') is strong contrast between light and shadow
questions.hint: The Italian word joins 'light' and 'dark'

feedback: Sfumato is soft, smoky blending, as in the Mona Lisa

questions.text: In a still life of a shiny apple, what is the brightest spot where light hits it directly called? Give the term.
questions.solution: A highlight is the brightest area, where light hits a surface most directly
questions.hint: It is the opposite of a shadow

questions.text: Which of these is a geometric shape?
questions.solution: Geometric shapes are regular, such as squares and circles; organic shapes are irregular, like leaves
questions.hint: Geometric shapes can be drawn with a ruler or compass

questions.text: Which arrangement creates symmetrical balance in a composition?
questions.solution: Symmetrical balance mirrors elements on either side of a central axis
questions.hint: Think about a mirror image

options: All the objects grouped in one corner
Random sizes scattered with no plan
One large object off-centre with nothing to balance it
Matching elements placed equally on either side of a central line

questions.text: In a two-point perspective drawing of a box, which statement is accurate?
questions.solution: In two-point perspective, verticals stay vertical and horizontal edges recede to two vanishing points
questions.hint: What happens to the upright edges?

options: Vertical edges stay vertical, and the other edges go towards two vanishing points on the horizon
All the edges go towards one vanishing point
Vertical edges go towards a third vanishing point
No edges go towards vanishing points

questions.text: A drawing of a mountain range shows the near hills dark and detailed and the far hills pale and blue. Which technique creates depth here?
questions.solution: Changes in colour, tone and detail with distance are aerial (atmospheric) perspective
questions.hint: Depth is shown by colour and detail, not by lines meeting

questions.text: An artist draws a vase by shading only the background around it, leaving the vase as blank paper. Which element are they using to show the vase?
questions.solution: Drawing the space around an object (negative space) makes the object's shape appear
questions.hint: The vase shows up only because of the shaded area that surrounds it

questions.text: Which shading technique changes gradually from light to dark with no hard edges? Give the term.
questions.solution: Blending (gradation) moves smoothly from light to dark
questions.hint: Think about a smooth change of tone, often smudged with a finger or a paper stump

feedback.bleeding: Bleeding is when wet colours run into each other — this shading technique changes tone smoothly

questions.text: Which statement about tone is accurate?
questions.solution: Shading with light and dark tones gives the illusion of form (3D)
questions.hint: Think about shading a circle so that it looks like a ball

options: Tone is only used in colour paintings
Tone means the outline of a shape
Adding tone can make a flat shape look three-dimensional

questions.text: An artist draws squares over a photo and matching squares on the paper to copy and enlarge it accurately. Give the name of this method.
questions.solution: The grid method (squaring up) helps copy and scale an image accurately, one square at a time
questions.hint: The squares form a network across the image

questions.text: Why do artists use aerial perspective in landscapes?
questions.solution: Aerial perspective imitates how air makes distant things look paler and bluer, creating depth
questions.hint: Think about how distant hills look on a hazy day

options: To create depth: distant objects are shown paler, cooler and less detailed
To make the foreground look flat
To show the view from an aeroplane
To make all objects the same size
feedback: 'Aerial' here refers to the air between the viewer and the distance

questions.text: Which statement about line is accurate?
questions.solution: Line is versatile: it can describe edges, suggest movement and build tone through hatching
questions.hint: Think of all the ways you use lines in a drawing

options: Line can show outline, movement, direction and tone, for example through hatching
Line is never used in painting

questions.text: Why might an artist place the main subject off-centre?
questions.solution: Placing the subject off-centre (often using the rule of thirds) can make a composition more dynamic
questions.hint: Think about the rule of thirds

options: An off-centre subject cannot be seen
Every artwork must follow this rule
An off-centre subject can create a more dynamic, interesting image than one in the middle
An off-centre subject removes the need for a focal point

questions.text: Why does foreshortening make a drawing look more realistic?
questions.solution: Our eyes see objects that point towards us as shortened; drawing them this way shows depth
questions.hint: Hold a pencil pointing at your eye: how long does it look?

options: All parts are drawn the same length
Parts pointing towards the viewer appear shorter, which matches how we see depth

questions.text: Which statement about organic and geometric shapes is accurate?
questions.solution: Organic shapes are free-flowing, like leaves; geometric shapes are regular and mathematical
questions.hint: Compare a leaf with a square

options: Organic shapes are irregular and found in nature; geometric shapes are regular, such as circles and squares
Geometric shapes are irregular and found in nature; organic shapes are regular
Geometric shapes cannot be used in art
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which principle of art is created by repeating lines, shapes or colours to suggest a visual beat? Give the term.
questions.solution: Repeating elements creates visual rhythm, which leads the eye through the work
questions.hint: The same word is used for the beat in music

questions.text: On the traditional painter's colour wheel, which are the primary colours?
questions.solution: On the traditional colour wheel used for paint, the primaries are red, yellow and blue
questions.hint: These colours cannot be made by mixing other paints

feedback: Red, green and blue are the primary colours of light (on screens)
These are the secondary colours

questions.text: Which colour is made by mixing blue and yellow paint?
questions.solution: Blue + yellow = green
questions.hint: Think of grass and leaves

feedback: Purple is red + blue
Orange is red + yellow

questions.text: What do you get when you add white to a colour? Give the term.
questions.solution: Adding white to a colour makes a tint, such as pink from red
questions.hint: Pastel colours are made this way

feedback.shade: A shade is made by adding black
feedback.tone: A tone is made by adding grey

questions.text: What do you get when you add black to a colour? Give the term.
questions.solution: Adding black to a colour makes a shade
questions.hint: It makes the colour darker

feedback.tint: A tint is made by adding white
feedback.tone: A tone is made by adding grey
feedback.shapes: Shape is a formal element, not a colour mix — check the spelling of the term for a colour plus black

questions.text: Which colours are warm colours?
questions.solution: Red, orange and yellow are warm colours, linked with fire and the sun
questions.hint: Think of fire and sunshine

feedback: These are cool colours

questions.text: What does 'hue' mean?
questions.solution: Hue is the pure colour itself, such as red, blue or yellow
questions.hint: Red, blue and yellow are each an example of one

options: How light or dark a colour is
The name of a pure colour, such as red or blue
feedback: That is a tint
That is a shade

questions.text: Which colour is opposite red on the colour wheel?
questions.solution: Red and green are complementary colours, opposite each other on the colour wheel
questions.hint: The opposite of a primary is the secondary made from the other two primaries

questions.text: Which statement about primary and secondary colours is accurate?
questions.solution: Primaries (red, yellow, blue) cannot be mixed; secondaries (orange, green, purple) are two primaries mixed
questions.hint: Can you mix red from other paints?

options: Secondary colours cannot be mixed from other colours; primaries are made by mixing two secondaries
Primary colours cannot be mixed from other colours; secondary colours are made by mixing two primaries
Primary and secondary colours are the same
Secondary colours are made by adding white
feedback: Adding white makes a tint

questions.text: What are colours that are opposite each other on the colour wheel called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Colours opposite each other on the wheel, such as red and green, are complementary
questions.hint: Each one 'completes' the other

feedback.analogous: Analogous colours are next to each other

questions.text: Which pair are complementary colours?
questions.solution: Blue and orange are opposite each other on the colour wheel
questions.hint: Find the colour directly opposite blue on the wheel

feedback: Blue and green are next to each other, so they are analogous

questions.text: What are colours that sit next to each other on the colour wheel, such as yellow, yellow-green and green, called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Colours next to each other on the wheel are analogous (harmonious) colours
questions.hint: They sit side by side and look calm together

feedback.complementary: Complementary colours are opposite each other

questions.text: Which of these is a tertiary colour?
questions.solution: A tertiary colour mixes a primary with a neighbouring secondary, such as blue-green
questions.hint: Tertiary colours often have two colour names joined by a hyphen

feedback: Green is a secondary colour
Blue is a primary colour

questions.text: Which of these is a cool colour?
questions.solution: Blue, green and purple are cool colours
questions.hint: Think of ice and water

questions.text: What happens when complementary colours are placed side by side?
questions.solution: Complementary colours side by side create strong contrast and make each other look more vivid
questions.hint: Think about red and green on a Christmas card

options: They make each other look duller
They make each other look brighter and stronger

questions.text: A painter wants a light pink. What should they do?
questions.solution: Pink is a tint of red, made by adding white
questions.hint: Which option would make red lighter, rather than darker or a different colour?

feedback: Adding black makes a darker shade, not pink

questions.text: A painting uses only tints and shades of blue. Which colour scheme is this?
questions.solution: A monochromatic scheme uses one hue with its tints and shades
questions.hint: 'Mono' means one

feedback: Analogous schemes use several neighbouring colours

questions.text: An artist wants a background to seem to go back into the distance. Which colours would help?
questions.solution: Cool and pale colours appear to recede, while warm, bright colours come forward
questions.hint: Think about distant hills on a hazy day

options: Cool, pale colours such as light blues
Bright, warm colours such as red and orange

questions.text: Mixing red and yellow paint makes which secondary colour? Give the colour.
questions.solution: Red + yellow = orange
questions.hint: Think of the colour of a sunset or a fruit

questions.text: Which kind of colour is made by mixing a primary colour with a neighbouring secondary colour, such as yellow with orange?
questions.solution: Primary + neighbouring secondary = tertiary colour, such as yellow-orange
questions.hint: It is the third type of colour on the wheel

questions.text: A poster designer wants text that contrasts strongly in colour with a purple background. Which colour gives the strongest colour contrast?
questions.solution: Yellow is opposite purple on the colour wheel, so it gives the strongest colour contrast
questions.hint: Find the complementary colour of purple

questions.text: Mixing two complementary colours, such as red and green paint, usually makes a dull colour. Give the colour.
questions.solution: Mixing complementary colours neutralises them, giving a brown or grey
questions.hint: The result is a dull, neutral colour

questions.text: Which colour scheme uses three colours evenly spaced around the colour wheel, such as red, yellow and blue?
questions.solution: A triadic scheme uses three colours evenly spaced around the wheel
questions.hint: 'Tri' means three

questions.text: A colour wheel has 12 colours: 3 primary, 3 secondary and the rest tertiary. How many tertiary colours are there?
questions.solution: 12 − 3 primary − 3 secondary = 6 tertiary colours
questions.hint: Subtract the primaries and secondaries from 12

questions.text: Which statement about tints, shades and tones is accurate?
questions.solution: Tint = colour + white; shade = colour + black; tone = colour + grey
questions.hint: Remember pink is a tint of red

options: A tint adds black, a shade adds white and a tone adds grey
A tint adds white, a shade adds black and a tone adds grey
A tint adds grey, a shade adds white and a tone adds black
Tints, shades and tones all add water

questions.text: On screens, colours are made by mixing light. Which are the primary colours of light?
questions.solution: Screens mix red, green and blue (RGB) light; all three together make white
questions.hint: Think of the letters RGB

feedback: Red, yellow and blue are the traditional primaries for mixing paint

questions.text: Which word describes how bright and pure a colour is, rather than dull and greyish? Give the term.
questions.solution: Saturation (intensity or chroma) is how pure and vivid a colour is
questions.hint: Photo-editing apps have a slider with this name that makes colours more vivid or more grey

questions.text: A painting shows orange flowers against a deep blue background. Why does this look so vibrant?
questions.solution: Complementary pairs placed together create the strongest colour contrast
questions.hint: Where are blue and orange on the colour wheel?

options: Blue and orange are analogous colours
Blue and orange are both warm colours
Blue and orange are both secondary colours
Blue and orange are complementary, so they intensify each other
feedback: Blue is a primary colour; orange is secondary

questions.text: Which secondary colour is the complementary colour of yellow? Give the colour.
questions.solution: Purple (violet) is opposite yellow on the colour wheel
questions.hint: Mix the two primaries that are not yellow

questions.text: Which statement about warm and cool colours is accurate?
questions.solution: Warm colours (reds, oranges) seem to advance; cool colours (blues, greens) seem to recede
questions.hint: Think about distant hills looking blue

options: Warm colours tend to come forward and cool colours tend to recede
Cool colours tend to come forward and warm colours tend to recede
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Why do printers use cyan, magenta, yellow and black inks (CMYK) instead of red, green and blue?
questions.solution: Printed inks subtract (absorb) light, so printing uses CMYK; screens add light, so they use RGB
questions.hint: Compare light coming from a screen with light bouncing off paper

options: Red, green and blue inks are banned
Inks absorb light (subtractive mixing), while screens add light together
CMYK uses fewer colours than RGB

questions.text: How did many Impressionist painters show shadows?
questions.solution: Many Impressionists avoided black and painted coloured shadows, often blue or violet
questions.hint: They noticed that shadows outdoors are often coloured

options: With grey pencil over the paint
With colours such as blues and violets instead of black

questions.text: Which statement about mixing paint is accurate?
questions.solution: Paint mixing is subtractive: mixing all the primaries gives a dark, muddy brown or near black
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a palette when every colour gets mixed

options: Mixing all three primary paints makes white
Mixing complementary colours makes a brighter colour
Adding white to a colour makes a shade
Mixing all three primary paints together tends to make a dark brown or near black
feedback: Mixing red, green and blue light makes white, but paint is different

questions.text: Black, white, grey and many browns are not strong hues on the colour wheel. What are these colours called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Neutral colours (black, white, grey, many browns and beiges) are not strong hues
questions.hint: Switzerland is often described with the same word, as it takes no side

questions.text: Which pair of colours gives the strongest tonal contrast?
questions.solution: Tonal contrast is the difference between light and dark; black and white are the extremes
questions.hint: Tonal contrast is about light and dark, not hue

questions.text: Which printmaking method involves cutting away parts of a surface so that the raised parts print?
questions.solution: In relief printing (lino or woodcut), the parts left standing take the ink and print
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the parts of the block that you do not cut away

options: Relief printing, such as lino printing
feedback: In etching, ink sits in lines below the surface (intaglio)

questions.text: Which drawing technique uses closely spaced parallel lines to build up tone? Give the term.
questions.solution: Hatching uses parallel lines; the closer together they are, the darker the tone
questions.hint: The lines all go in the same direction and do not cross

feedback.cross-hatching: Cross-hatching adds lines that cross the first set

questions.text: What is collage?
questions.solution: Collage comes from the French 'coller', to stick: materials are glued onto a surface
questions.hint: The name comes from the French word for glue

options: Artwork made by sticking materials such as paper and fabric onto a surface

questions.text: Which pencil grade is the softest and makes the darkest marks?
questions.solution: B pencils are soft and dark; the higher the B number, the softer and darker: 6B is softer than 2B
questions.hint: B stands for black; the higher the number, the darker

feedback: H pencils are hard and make light marks
HB is in the middle

questions.text: Which drawing technique uses lots of small dots to build up tone? Give the term.
questions.solution: Stippling builds tone with dots: more dots close together give darker tone
questions.hint: It is done with the tip of a pen, dot by dot

questions.text: What is a kiln used for?
questions.solution: A kiln is a very hot oven that fires clay to make it hard and permanent
questions.hint: It is a very hot oven

options: Firing clay at very high temperatures

questions.text: Which paint is water-based, dries quickly and becomes waterproof when dry?
questions.solution: Acrylic is water-based, dries quickly and is waterproof once dry
questions.hint: It is a modern paint made with a plastic binder

feedback: Oil paint dries slowly and is not water-based
Watercolour can be re-wetted after drying

questions.text: Which statement about hatching and cross-hatching is accurate?
questions.solution: Hatching is parallel lines; cross-hatching layers crossing lines to build darker tones
questions.hint: The word 'cross' gives a clue

options: Cross-hatching uses parallel lines; hatching adds lines that cross over them
Hatching uses parallel lines; cross-hatching adds more lines that cross over them
Both mean blending with a finger
feedback: Dots are stippling

questions.text: Which painting technique applies paint so thickly that brush or knife marks stand out from the surface? Give the term.
questions.solution: Impasto is very thick paint that keeps the marks of the brush or knife, as in Van Gogh's work
questions.hint: Van Gogh used it in his skies

questions.text: Which technique scratches through a top layer to reveal a different colour underneath?
questions.solution: Sgraffito (Italian for 'scratched') scratches through one layer to show the layer below
questions.hint: The name comes from the Italian for 'scratched'

feedback: Frottage is taking a rubbing of a textured surface

questions.text: Which technique involves placing paper over a textured surface and rubbing with a crayon or pencil? Give the term.
questions.solution: Frottage (from the French for 'rubbing') was used by Max Ernst
questions.hint: It comes from the French for 'to rub'

questions.text: Which statement about additive and subtractive sculpture is accurate?
questions.solution: Additive means adding material (modelling, construction); subtractive means taking it away (carving)
questions.hint: Think about adding and subtracting

options: Subtractive sculpture builds up material; additive sculpture removes material
Additive sculpture builds up material, such as modelling clay; subtractive sculpture removes material, such as carving
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which watercolour technique adds wet paint onto wet paper so that colours spread and blend?
questions.solution: Wet-on-wet lets colours flow into each other with soft edges
questions.hint: Both the paper and the paint are wet

questions.text: What is the liquid clay used like glue to join pieces of clay together called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Slip is clay mixed with water to a creamy liquid, used with scoring to join clay
questions.hint: It is used after scoring both surfaces

questions.text: An artist cuts some lettering into a lino block. When it is printed, how will the lettering appear?
questions.solution: Printing flips the image, so lettering must be cut in reverse to read correctly
questions.hint: Think about stamping a rubber stamp onto paper

questions.text: A student wants a soft, smudgy drawing with rich blacks that can be blended with a finger. Which medium is most suitable?
questions.solution: Charcoal gives rich, dark marks that blend and smudge easily
questions.hint: It is made from burnt wood

feedback: 2H is a hard pencil that makes light marks

questions.text: A student paints a sky by laying a smooth, even layer of thinned watercolour across the paper. What is this technique called?
questions.solution: An even layer of thinned watercolour is a flat wash
questions.hint: The paint is thinned with lots of water and spread evenly

questions.text: Before using clay, potters knead it to remove air bubbles that could make it crack or explode in the kiln. Give the term for this process.
questions.solution: Wedging removes air bubbles and makes the clay even
questions.hint: It is a special word for kneading clay, beginning with 'w'

questions.text: A student prints several colours from one lino block, cutting away more of it after each colour. What is this called?
questions.solution: In a reduction print, the same block is cut away further for each colour
questions.hint: The block gets smaller (reduced) each time

questions.text: Which tool is used to roll ink evenly onto a printing block?
questions.solution: A brayer is a hand roller that spreads ink evenly over the block
questions.hint: You push it back and forth over a slab of ink, then over the block

feedback: A baren is used to rub the back of the paper to transfer the ink
A gouge is used to cut the lino

questions.text: What is the name of the internal frame, often made of wire, that supports a clay or papier-mâché sculpture? Give the term.
questions.solution: An armature is an internal support frame for a sculpture
questions.hint: It works like a skeleton inside the sculpture

questions.text: A student wants to keep pure white highlights in a watercolour painting. What should they do?
questions.solution: In watercolour the white comes from the paper, so highlights are left unpainted or protected with masking fluid
questions.hint: Watercolour is transparent, so the whites come from the paper

options: Paint over them with black first
Add white acrylic to every colour
Leave the paper unpainted in those areas or use masking fluid

questions.text: Two clay pieces are joined but fall apart when they dry. Which step was most likely missed?
questions.solution: Clay joins need scoring and slip to bond properly
questions.hint: Think about how clay pieces are glued together

options: Scoring both surfaces and using slip

questions.text: Which list shows the stages of making a glazed ceramic pot in the correct order?
questions.solution: Clay is shaped, dried, bisque (biscuit) fired, glazed and then fired again
questions.hint: The clay must be shaped and dried before it goes in the kiln

options: Shape the clay, dry to bone dry, bisque fire, glaze, glaze fire
Glaze, shape the clay, bisque fire, dry, glaze fire
Bisque fire, shape the clay, glaze, dry, glaze fire
Shape the clay, glaze fire, dry, bisque fire, glaze

questions.text: An artist pushes ink through a fine mesh with a stencil blocking some areas. Which process is this, famously used by Andy Warhol?
questions.solution: Screen printing pushes ink through a mesh screen; a stencil blocks some areas
questions.hint: Warhol used it to repeat images of celebrities

questions.text: Which group of printmaking processes holds the ink in lines cut or scratched into a metal plate, such as etching? Give the term.
questions.solution: In intaglio printing (etching, engraving, drypoint), ink is held in lines below the surface
questions.hint: The word is Italian and begins with 'in'

feedback.relief: Relief prints from the raised surface, not from cut lines

questions.text: Why is fixative sprayed on charcoal and pastel drawings?
questions.solution: Fixative holds loose charcoal or pastel dust in place so the drawing does not smudge
questions.hint: Charcoal and pastel rub off easily

options: To make the paper waterproof for painting

questions.text: Which statement about oil paint compared with acrylic paint is accurate?
questions.solution: Oil paint dries slowly, allowing long blending time; acrylic dries quickly and cleans up with water
questions.hint: Think about drying time

options: Oil paint dries faster than acrylic
Oil paint is cleaned up with water
Acrylic can never be used thickly
Oil paint dries much more slowly, so it can be blended for longer
feedback: Oil paint needs solvents such as white spirit

questions.text: Why might a student choose acrylic rather than oil paint for a project with a short deadline?
questions.solution: Acrylic dries fast, so layers can be added quickly, and brushes clean with water
questions.hint: Think about drying time and cleaning up

options: Acrylic dries quickly and cleans up with water

questions.text: Which statement about monoprinting is accurate?
questions.solution: 'Mono' means one: monoprinting usually makes a single, unique print
questions.hint: 'Mono' means one

options: A monoprint always produces hundreds of identical prints
A monoprint usually produces one unique print rather than identical copies
A monoprint is a type of sculpture

questions.text: Why do potters fire clay in a kiln?
questions.solution: Firing permanently changes clay into hard ceramic that cannot be softened with water again
questions.hint: Think about what happens to unfired clay if it gets wet

options: The heat makes the clay soft for reshaping
The high heat changes the clay permanently so it becomes hard and durable
The heat turns clay into metal

questions.text: Why might an artist use mixed media in an artwork?
questions.solution: Mixed media combines different materials to create richer textures and effects
questions.hint: Think about combining collage, paint and drawing

options: Mixed media is the only way to show perspective
Mixed media stops the work being judged
Mixed media makes every artwork waterproof
Combining materials can add texture and variety that one medium alone cannot

questions.text: Which fabric technique uses melted wax to stop dye soaking into parts of the cloth and is traditional in Indonesia? Give the name.
questions.solution: Batik uses wax as a resist so that dye cannot reach the waxed areas
questions.hint: The name is an Indonesian word

questions.text: A sculptor wants to make several identical bronze copies of a clay sculpture. Which process is used?
questions.solution: Bronze sculptures are made by casting molten metal in a mould taken from the original
questions.hint: Think about how one original shape can be copied many times in metal

questions.text: Which term describes paint that lets light pass through it so the layers underneath show, as with watercolour? Give the term.
questions.solution: Watercolour is transparent, so earlier layers and the white paper show through
questions.hint: It is the opposite of opaque

feedback.opaque: Opaque paint covers what is underneath, like gouache

questions.text: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.solution: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa in the early 1500s, during the Italian Renaissance
questions.hint: He was an Italian Renaissance artist who was also an inventor

questions.text: Which art movement is Claude Monet linked with?
questions.solution: Monet was a leading Impressionist; his painting Impression, Sunrise gave the movement its name
questions.hint: One of his paintings gave the movement its name

questions.text: Which Spanish artist developed Cubism with Georges Braque? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque developed Cubism from about 1907
questions.hint: His first name is Pablo

questions.text: Which artist painted The Persistence of Memory, with its melting clocks?
questions.solution: Salvador Dalí, a Surrealist, painted The Persistence of Memory (1931)
questions.hint: He was a Spanish Surrealist with a famous curled moustache

feedback: Magritte was also a Surrealist, but he did not paint the melting clocks

questions.text: Which Pop artist made famous prints of Campbell's soup cans? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Andy Warhol made Campbell's Soup Cans (1962) and many screen prints
questions.hint: His first name is Andy

questions.text: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.solution: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512
questions.hint: He also carved the famous statue of David

questions.text: Which artist painted The Starry Night?
questions.solution: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889
questions.hint: This Dutch artist also painted Sunflowers

questions.text: Which feature is typical of Impressionism?
questions.solution: Impressionists used quick, visible brushstrokes to capture light and atmosphere, often outdoors
questions.hint: Think of Monet painting the same haystacks at different times of day

options: Visible brushstrokes capturing changing light, often painted outdoors
Geometric shapes showing several viewpoints at once
feedback: That describes Surrealism
That describes Pop Art
That describes Cubism

questions.text: Which feature is typical of Cubism?
questions.solution: Cubism breaks subjects into geometric planes and shows several viewpoints at the same time
questions.hint: The name comes from 'cubes'

options: Objects broken into geometric shapes and shown from several viewpoints at once
feedback: That describes Jackson Pollock's Abstract Expressionism

questions.text: Which art movement of the 1920s explored dreams and the unconscious mind, with artists such as Dalí and Magritte? Give the movement.
questions.solution: Surrealism explored dreams and the unconscious from the 1920s
questions.hint: The name means 'beyond realism'

questions.text: Which Pop artist used comic-strip images and Ben-Day dots?
questions.solution: Roy Lichtenstein painted large comic-strip images with Ben-Day dots, such as Whaam! (1963)
questions.hint: His most famous painting is called Whaam!

questions.text: Which American painter is famous for 'drip' paintings and is linked with Abstract Expressionism? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Jackson Pollock dripped and poured paint onto canvases laid on the floor
questions.hint: His first name is Jackson

questions.text: Which Norwegian artist painted The Scream? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Edvard Munch painted The Scream (1893), an important influence on Expressionism
questions.hint: His surname has five letters and sounds like 'monk'

questions.text: Which period saw a 'rebirth' of classical art and learning in Italy, with artists such as Leonardo and Raphael?
questions.solution: The Renaissance (French for 'rebirth') began in Italy in the 14th–15th centuries
questions.hint: The name is French for 'rebirth'

questions.text: A painting shows everyday consumer products in bright, flat colours and was made by screen printing. Which movement is it most likely from?
questions.solution: Images of consumer products, bright flat colour and screen printing are typical of Pop Art
questions.hint: Think of Andy Warhol

questions.text: A painting is made of tiny dots of pure colour placed side by side, which blend when seen from a distance. Which technique is this?
questions.solution: Pointillism, developed by Georges Seurat, uses dots of pure colour that mix in the viewer's eye
questions.hint: Georges Seurat developed this technique

questions.text: A painting uses strong, unnatural colours and distorted shapes to express feelings rather than show reality. Which movement is it most likely from?
questions.solution: Expressionism distorts colour and form to express emotion
questions.hint: The name of the movement is about expressing feelings

questions.text: Which British sculptor made the Angel of the North? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Antony Gormley's Angel of the North (1998) stands in Gateshead
questions.hint: His first name is Antony

questions.text: Which artist is known for large, smooth sculptures of reclining figures with holes through them?
questions.solution: Henry Moore is famous for his reclining figures with hollows and holes
questions.hint: He was a British sculptor from Yorkshire

feedback: Rodin is famous for The Thinker

questions.text: Which Japanese artist made the woodblock print The Great Wave off Kanagawa? Give the name.
questions.solution: Katsushika Hokusai made The Great Wave off Kanagawa in about 1831
questions.hint: He was a Japanese printmaker famous for his views of Mount Fuji

questions.text: Which art movement of the 1910s rejected traditional art, using nonsense and everyday 'readymade' objects?
questions.solution: Dada began during the First World War and rejected traditional ideas of art
questions.hint: Its name is a nonsense word

questions.text: Which list puts these art movements in time order, earliest first?
questions.solution: Renaissance (1400s–1500s), Impressionism (1870s), Cubism (from about 1907), Pop Art (1950s–60s)
questions.hint: Start with the oldest, which was in Italy hundreds of years ago

questions.text: A painting by Monet gave its name to Impressionism. What was it called?
questions.solution: Monet's Impression, Sunrise (1872) led a critic to call the group 'Impressionists'
questions.hint: It shows the harbour at Le Havre in hazy early-morning light

feedback: Water Lilies is a later series by Monet
The Starry Night is by Van Gogh

questions.text: Which statement about the Renaissance is accurate?
questions.solution: Renaissance artists studied the human body and used linear perspective for realism
questions.hint: Think about Leonardo's drawings of the human body

options: Artists studied anatomy and used linear perspective to create realistic space
Artists rejected realism for flat geometric shapes
Renaissance artists mainly used screen printing

questions.text: Which statement correctly compares Impressionism and Expressionism?
questions.solution: Impressionism captured light and atmosphere; Expressionism distorted colour and form to show feelings
questions.hint: Look at the words 'impression' and 'expression'

options: Expressionists focused on capturing light; Impressionists focused on showing emotion
Impressionists focused on capturing light and the moment; Expressionists focused on showing emotion
Both movements began in the Renaissance
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which Dutch artist painted grids of black lines with blocks of primary colour and is linked with De Stijl? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Piet Mondrian used black grids and red, yellow and blue blocks
questions.hint: His first name is Piet

questions.text: Which movement includes Mark Rothko's large fields of colour and Jackson Pollock's action painting?
questions.solution: Rothko and Pollock were Abstract Expressionists working in New York in the 1940s and 1950s
questions.hint: Both artists worked in New York after the Second World War

questions.text: Which artist painted The Kiss, using gold leaf?
questions.solution: Gustav Klimt painted The Kiss (1907–1908) in Vienna, using gold leaf
questions.hint: He worked in Vienna, Austria

questions.text: Why is Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon (1907) seen as important?
questions.solution: Its flattened, angular figures broke with traditional perspective and paved the way for Cubism
questions.hint: Which movement did Picasso develop soon afterwards?

options: The painting broke with traditional perspective and led towards Cubism
The painting was the first Impressionist work
The painting was the first Pop Art screen print

questions.text: Which statement about Pop Art is accurate?
questions.solution: Pop Art (1950s–60s, Britain and the USA) drew on advertising, comics and celebrity
questions.hint: 'Pop' is short for 'popular'

options: Pop Art began in Renaissance Italy
Pop Art used images from advertising, comics and mass media and began in Britain and the USA in the 1950s
Pop Art avoided popular culture completely
Pop Art only used marble sculpture

questions.text: Why did the Impressionists often paint outdoors (en plein air)?
questions.solution: Painting outdoors let them record light and atmosphere as it changed
questions.hint: What were the Impressionists most interested in?

options: To capture the changing effects of natural light directly

questions.text: Which statement about Surrealism is accurate?
questions.solution: Surrealists painted dreamlike, illogical scenes, often in a very realistic style
questions.hint: Think of Dalí's melting clocks

options: Surrealists painted only realistic portraits of royalty
Surrealism was mainly about capturing light outdoors
Surrealism used only geometric grids of primary colours
Surrealists explored dreams and the unconscious, often combining realistic detail with strange, illogical scenes
feedback: That describes Mondrian and De Stijl

questions.text: Which statement about Andy Goldsworthy's work is accurate?
questions.solution: Goldsworthy creates temporary sculptures from natural materials outdoors and photographs them
questions.hint: His works are often outdoors and do not last long

options: He makes land art from natural materials such as leaves, stones and ice, often recorded in photographs
He makes comic-strip paintings with Ben-Day dots

questions.text: Which technique, whose name comes from the Italian for 'smoke', blends tones softly without hard outlines, as in the Mona Lisa? Give the term.
questions.solution: Sfumato (from the Italian for 'smoke') blends tones softly, as Leonardo did in the Mona Lisa
questions.hint: Leonardo da Vinci was famous for this soft blending

feedback.chiaroscuro: Chiaroscuro is strong contrast between light and dark

questions.text: Why did Cubist artists show objects from several viewpoints at once?
questions.solution: Cubists wanted to show more of an object than a single viewpoint allows, rethinking traditional perspective
questions.hint: Think about seeing the front and side of a face at the same time

options: To make paintings look exactly like photographs
To represent the whole object on a flat surface rather than copying a single view
To show the effect of light at different times of day
feedback: That was the aim of Impressionists such as Monet
